claim: Nine spec sites still present the dissolved `impact` and `emit` modules as current. The defect this report is keyed to is the declared description of data_flow `1d33b4c6c36e` (Proposal lifecycle) in spec/proposal/module.json:93: "Proposal file -> register (...) -> spec change -> impact -> bead actions -> history query." The others: spec/merkle/arch_tree_builder.md:72 ("so impact never sees it, emit ..."), spec/ingest/arch_refresh.md:107 ("derived by negating impact's bead-producing types"), spec/proposal/arch_proposal_commands.md:39 ("the same as impact's `--beads` input"), spec/ingest/test_reconciliation.md:139 ("emit's real ordering"), and four weaker sites left for triage judgment: spec/schema/arch_bead_map_schema.md:42 ("impact analysis joins ..."), spec/map/arch_mapping_store.md:52 (a journal-line example whose `path` is `impact/arch_action_classifier.md` while its `proposal` is `2026-08-13-plan-module`), spec/merkle/arch_completeness_checker.md:37 (an error-message example whose module reads `(impact)`), spec/proposal/arch_history_viewer.md:85 (example output carrying the bead title `emit: ChangesetBuilder`).
authoritative_source: Proposal 2026-08-13-plan-module: `spex impact` and `spex emit` are removed and `spex plan` added, and "the pipeline reads validate -> diff -> plan -> adapter -> ingest everywhere it is written down". The plan module is the live successor: spec/plan/module.json declares ActionClassifier, ChangesetBuilder and the rest, and spec/project.json lists no `impact` or `emit` module.
evidence: Each site names a module that no longer exists as the current actor, so a reader following the leaf is sent to a directory that is gone (spec/impact/, spec/emit/) or told a stage runs that does not. The removal-time name sweep cannot catch them: it recovers a removed node's declared NAME, and the retired api names `spex impact` / `spex emit` were swept successfully -- what survives is the bare module word. scripts/lens-lexicon.sh cannot catch them either: it matches only terms declared under a proposal's "## Retired vocabulary" heading, and 2026-08-13-plan-module declares the command spellings (`spex impact`, `spex emit`, `ImpactCommand`, ...) but never the bare module names `impact` and `emit`. The lens therefore reports "corpus clean of all retired vocabulary" over a corpus holding these nine sites, which is how they survived the epic's own sweep.
proposed_fix: Rewrite the six clear sites onto the plan module and triage the remaining three as examples (a historical bead title and two illustrative outputs may legitimately name a module that existed). Separately, and outside the spec: declare the bare module names under the plan-module proposal's "## Retired vocabulary" heading so scripts/lens-lexicon.sh can see this class at all -- without that the gate keeps reporting clean over the same defect. Note lens-lexicon.sh greps only spec/ *.md and *.json, so the repo-wide half of this class stays a manual sweep either way.
